name: Provisioned Google user can create and retain a bid
description: Verifies an authorized Google identity can enter BidWatch, create a bid and see the resulting operational dashboard.
steps: Sign in with the provisioned Google account
Open Add bid and enter title "Network Security RFP", organisation "Example Org", and a deadline 10 days in the future
expected: The provisioned user enters BidWatch, the bid persists, and permitted KPI cards are visible without exposing restricted administration metrics.

name: Destructive deletion preserves a text-only bid history record
description: Verifies an irreversible bid deletion requires explicit confirmation and preserves the bid metadata after stored documents are removed.
setup: Create a bid titled "Historical RFP" with organisation "Example Org" and a small PDF attachment
steps: Review the impact message and choose Keep it
Choose Delete bid and documents again
Choose Delete bid in the confirmation dialog
expected: The bid disappears from active bids, its stored document is removed, and a text-only history record remains with the bid title, organisation, deadline, status and deletion date.

name: Protected workflow transitions require their own permissions
description: Verifies ordinary bid editing cannot bypass dedicated Applied or Declined permissions.
setup: Create an open bid while signed in as an authorized bid contributor
steps: Sign in as a role without bids.apply or bids.decline
Attempt to change its status to Applied or Declined through the normal application flow
expected: The protected transitions are unavailable or rejected by the backend; ordinary edit permission cannot elevate into submission authority.

name: Sensitive roles cannot be self-escalated
description: Verifies non-Super-Admin access managers cannot grant sensitive access-control permissions.
steps: Sign in as a non-Super-Admin user with role-management capability
Create or edit a custom role and attempt to include users.manage, roles.manage, or settings.manage
Attempt to assign a sensitive role
expected: The backend rejects sensitive permission allocation or assignment and the protected Super Admin remains the only authority for sensitive access.

name: Production errors are actionable without exposing internals
description: Verifies a simulated server failure is surfaced as a concise user-facing error rather than a blank screen or technical stack trace.
steps: Submit while the server returns the simulated 500 response
expected: The UI shows a plain-language failure message and does not display the injected stack trace or internal implementation details.
